title: EMOSA fleet configuration
description: The front port every pod is handed to, and the settings every agent it creates inherits.

advertise.description: Host the pods reach agent ports on; manager_addr becomes tcp:ADVERTISE:PORT.

forward.description: The package's forwarder (emosa-forward-c) exposes the front port and the agent ports, which listen on loopback, on the advertise address (an IPv4 address, a gateway's LAN address) where the pods reach them. Default false: another forwarder does (in the labs, an LXD proxy).

phy_netdev_up.description: spec 3.10, on by default: on a legacy pod with radio_plan emosa, one Wifi_Inet_Config row (if_type tap, enabled, network, ip_assign_scheme none, NAT off) for each radio carrying a home AP whose VIFs are all EMOSA's, with no VIF or Inet row on its own netdev, so nm sets that netdev up; false, the tap rows on the pod's radios removed.

uplink.description: Given to every agent. Data plane option 1: the agent switches the pod's backhaul station onto the EasyMesh backhaul (data-plane.md §5.3, spec §8). Mode ethernet: a wired pod's uplink port bridged into br-home (spec §8.4). Absent or mode off: the pod keeps its OpenSync uplink (option 2).

mode.description: multi-ap: option 1 (spec §8.3); ethernet: a wired pod, its Ethernet uplink bridged into the fronthaul's bridge (spec §8.4); gre: a GRE-parent child steered onto a parent AP by BSSID, no configured upstream (spec §8.6).

port.description: With mode ethernet: the pod's Ethernet uplink port.

credentials.description: m2: the backhaul BSS of the controller's applied M2 set (multi_bss); config: ssid and secret_ref below.

secret_ref.description: A file in the agent's secret directory (state_dir/secrets), mode 0600.

bootstrap.description: A legacy pod's station on the site's GTP BSS (spec 3.10, the GTP station): written once per start of its OpenSync while the station has no row. Any mode a legacy pod serves.

secret_ref.description: Its WPA2-PSK passphrase: a file in the agent's secret directory (state_dir/secrets), mode 0600.

bssid.description: A pin to one GTP BSS (parent), none by default: a pinned pod stays on that BSS when the site's GTP BSS changes.

unassociated_seconds.description: The station's guard: the station in EMOSA's form not associated this long is deleted (spec 3.10: the pods' vendor healthcheck reboots a pod after ten minutes of an unassociated station). 300 by default.

retry_seconds.description: The back-off before the station is written again after each removal, the last repeated: 900, 1800, 3600 by default; back to the first once a write associates.

bssid.description: The upstream backhaul BSS the station is pinned to, required with mode multi-ap. Never one of the pod's own BSSIDs: a station on its own backhaul BSS loops br-home.

hold_backoff.description: Seconds a failed switch holds the pod on option 2 before the switch is made again (spec §8.3), doubled with each held retry.

hold_backoff_cap.description: The longest hold between two retries, in seconds.

kept_tries.description: A kept backhaul target on another fleet pod (spec §8.3): the switches made to it with that pod's AP up before it is given up.

kept_backoff.description: Seconds before such a target is tried again after a failed switch, doubled after each.

parent_wait_cap.description: The longest a kept target waits for its fleet pod's AP to be up before it is given up, in seconds.

telemetry.description: Given to every agent (each subscribes to its own pod's topic). The pod's own statistics (spec §3.6): the agent sets the pod's MQTT settings and a raw client report once per OpenSync start, and subscribes to the pod's topic. Absent or mode off: the agent leaves the pod's statistics publishing alone.

broker.description: Broker host the pod connects to (mutual TLS with its device certificate).

subscribe.description: host:port where the agent reads the pod's topic.

publish_interval.description: qm's publish interval in seconds (mqtt_settings agg_stats_interval). Absent: OpenSync's default, 60 s.

survey.description: Also a raw on-channel survey of the radio (channel utilization for AP metrics, spec 3.8).

topology_query_window.description: Given to every agent: a property of the controller (spec §2.5). Absent: the rule is off.

gtp_underlay.description: The site's own GTP underlay (spec 8.2), such as 169.254.1.0/24: given, the registry allocates each pod an underlay for its role as a GRE parent (spec 8.6), a 169.254.N.0/24 that never overlaps this one. Absent: none.

secrets.description: The fleet's own secret store (a directory, mode 0700, one private file per reference): a secret_ref an agent configuration names (its uplink's, its GTP station's) that the agent's store lacks is copied from here when the fleet writes the configuration; never replaced, never logged by value (spec 4).

files.description: The fleet's file server (spec 4, the pods' modules): plain HTTP on the advertise address only. GET or HEAD / answers 200 with an empty body; GET /<sha256> a file of directory whose name is the SHA-256 of its content (checked at the fleet's start; others are not served), 404 otherwise. Every reply carries a Date header (GMT) while the gateway's clock is synchronized; each request is logged. Absent: no server, and no module update.

directory.description: The files served, each named by its SHA-256 (lowercase hex), at most 1 MiB each.

time_synced_command.description: A shell command whose exit status 0 says the gateway's clock is synchronized (a platform whose time daemon does not keep the kernel's clock status). Absent: the kernel's clock status (adjtimex). While the clock is not synchronized no reply carries a Date and GET or HEAD / is 503.

modules.description: Settings for modules of the pods' own software (spec 4, the pods' modules), by module name (the site's: a pod-side hook's, say; emosa is EMOSA's own, a legacy pod's start marker, spec 3.10): each agent writes its module's Node_Config rows and reports its Node_State. pods.<serial>.modules replaces it for one pod.

config.description: The module's settings, key to value (a Node_Config row each). update_url and update_sha256 are the fleet's, from update.

update.description: A file for the module to install, by its SHA-256: a file of files.directory named so. The agent's settings get update_url (the fleet's file server, on its advertise address) and update_sha256.

run_root.description: Each agent's run directory is run_root/<pod_id> (its status, on a RAM disk on a gateway). Absent: the agents write their status in their state directories.

admit_by_model.description: The router's admit switch (spec 4, the pods' models): on, the fleet admits every pod one of its models recognises, whatever admit lists; off (the default), only admit's.

models.description: The pod models the fleet knows, in order of preference (spec 4, the pods' models): the first whose model equals the pod's AWLAN_Node model and whose firmware_prefix, when given, starts its firmware_version recognises it, and its settings apply to the pod unless pods.<serial> sets them.

agents.description: How the agents run (spec §4). systemd: an emosa-agent@POD unit each, enabled and started by the fleet. supervised: the C fleet's own children, for a system without systemd (a router's busybox init): the link helper, then the agent, with /etc/default/emosa and /etc/default/emosa-POD in their environment, started again 3 s after one ends, stopped when its pod is forgotten and when the fleet ends; each one's output in LOG_ROOT/POD/agent.log (the run root, else the state root), kept to two files of 256 KiB. Absent: EMOSA_AGENTS from the fleet's environment or /etc/default/emosa, else systemd.

pods.description: Per-pod overrides of the agent settings above, by serial number.

vif.description: Ignored; the fronthaul VIF comes from the profile.
